# Calculating ∫ -3*x**4*cos(x) dx

I'll use **integration by parts** with the tabular method (repeated application).

## Setting up the tabular method

| Differentiate (u) | Integrate (dv) | Sign |
|---|---|---|
| -3*x**4 | cos(x) | + |
| -12*x**3 | sin(x) | − |
| -36*x**2 | -cos(x) | + |
| -72*x | -sin(x) | − |
| -72 | cos(x) | + |
| 0 | sin(x) | |

## Multiplying diagonally (alternating signs)

| Term | Calculation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | (+)(-3*x**4)(sin(x)) | -3*x**4*sin(x) |
| 2 | (−)(-12*x**3)(-cos(x)) | -12*x**3*cos(x) |
| 3 | (+)(-36*x**2)(-sin(x)) | 36*x**2*sin(x) |
| 4 | (−)(-72*x)(cos(x)) | 72*x*cos(x) |
| 5 | (+)(-72)(sin(x)) | -72*sin(x) |

## Result

$$\int -3x^4 \cos(x)\,dx = -3x^4\sin(x) - 12x^3\cos(x) + 36x^2\sin(x) + 72x\cos(x) - 72\sin(x) + C$$

## Verification (differentiating back)

- d/dx[-3*x**4*sin(x)] = -12*x**3*sin(x) - 3*x**4*cos(x)
- d/dx[-12*x**3*cos(x)] = -36*x**2*cos(x) + 12*x**3*sin(x)
- d/dx[36*x**2*sin(x)] = 72*x*sin(x) + 36*x**2*cos(x)
- d/dx[72*x*cos(x)] = 72*cos(x) - 72*x*sin(x)
- d/dx[-72*sin(x)] = -72*cos(x)

All terms cancel except **−3*x**4*cos(x)** ✓

<answer>-3*x**4*sin(x) - 12*x**3*cos(x) + 36*x**2*sin(x) + 72*x*cos(x) - 72*sin(x) + C</answer>
